title: Python SDK: stream orchestrator + checkpoint hooks and telemetry ergonomics
creator: Sofia Mendes
description:
Goal: design and ship a developer-friendly Python SDK primitive for streaming chat that unifies (1) an async iterator + context-manager surface for simple consumption, (2) explicit checkpoint/resume semantics for reconnects and long-lived consumers, and (3) telemetry hooks and backpressure signals that integrate with Redwood Console traces and cost reporting. This ticket focuses on API ergonomics, runtime behavior, and an example app for resumable live transcription and multi-consumer fanout.

Motivation:
- Customers build streaming chat UIs and server-side aggregators; reconnect and duplication are common pain points.
- Current examples and helpers are scattered; we need a single idiomatic surface that handles retries, idempotency, checkpoint tokens, and emits rich telemetry without leaking complexity to callers.

Non-goals:
- Full backwards-compatibility with older sync-only SDK primitives (we can provide adapters).
- Implementing the network protocol server-side (runtime already emits tokens/events)

Deliverables:
- New Python primitive: StreamOrchestrator (async context manager) + ConversationCursor (opaque resume token).
- Reference example: resumable-live-transcribe.py demonstrating consumer restart and dedup semantics.
- Telemetry hooks: on_chunk, on_resume, on_lag, on_backpressure with lightweight tracing metadata consumed by Console.
- Unit + integration tests and a small benchmark that exercises reconnect under load.

Design notes and API sketch:
1) Household API (high-level):
   async with StreamOrchestrator(client.chat.stream(...), on_telemetry=hook) as orchestrator:
       async for event in orchestrator.consume():
           if isinstance(event, MessageDelta):
               render(event.text)
           elif isinstance(event, Checkpoint):
               save_cursor(event.cursor)

   - consume() returns an async iterator of normalized events (MessageDelta, FinalMessage, Checkpoint, Heartbeat, ErrorEvent).
   - Checkpoint contains an opaque string cursor that the runtime accepts on reconnect to fast-forward the stream (server-authored).

2) Resume semantics:
   - Orchestrator accepts resume_cursor and resume_policy (strict|fuzzy|drop-duplicates).
   - On reconnect, orchestrator requests resume and reconciles events using per-event ids to dedupe overlapping content.
   - Client-side checkpoints are optional but recommended for long-running sessions or mobile cold-starts.

3) Backpressure and batching:
   - The orchestrator exposes a backpressure_zero() callback so callers can signal they are saturated (SDK will request smaller server-side batch or pause delivery).
   - Default behavior: flow-control window = 16 in-flight deltas, configurable via StreamConfig.

4) Telemetry hooks and Console integration:
   - Minimal hook signature: def on_telemetry(kind: str, payload: Dict[str, Any]) (we will provide typed wrappers).
   - Events: token_watermark, resume_latency_ms, reconnect_attempt, duplicate_suppressed, backpressure_entered/exited.
   - SDK emits trace_id and route/model metadata to link with Console traces and cost breakdowns.

Trade-offs considered:
- Server-issued resume tokens vs client offsets: server tokens avoid schema drift and partial-message ambiguity but require runtime support. We choose server tokens for reliability; fallback to client-offsets supported for edge cases.
- Opaque events vs typed objects: typed objects are more ergonomic but require versioning. We will version event envelope and include schema_version on each event.
- Aggressive dedupe on client vs relying on server: doing client-side dedupe allows resilience when intermediate proxies drop messages, at cost of extra state. We'll implement lightweight dedupe by event-id TTL (configurable).

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- API landed with docs and typed stubs (py.typed).
- Reference example in examples/ that demonstrates resume after a simulated network drop and shows no duplicated tokens in output.
- Telemetry events are visible in a dev Console trace (link to dev dashboard in comments).
acceptance_criteria: Async context manager + async iterator primitive implemented and exported from redwood_sdk.streams
Checkpoint resume roundtrip works in integration tests (simulate disconnect and resume_cursor reuse)
Backpressure signals pause/resume delivery and are covered by unit tests
Telemetry hooks emit trace_id and appear in dev Console traces
Example app added to examples/resumable_live_transcribe.py demonstrating restart semantics

comments: 2026-02-20 Sofia Mendes: Kickoff - initial design and API sketch above. Blocking questions: exact resume token format (opaque string or JSON) and whether runtime will support client-side cursors. Posted question to infra-runtime channel.

2026-02-24 Arjun Patel: Added default flow-control window and initial event envelope shape. Decided to include schema_version and event_id for dedupe. Will prototype dedupe using a small LRU cache with TTL.

2026-03-02 Design review (Ava Liu): UX feedback - prefer a single consume() iterator rather than multiple callback flavors; also suggested a high-level convenience helper that returns a buffered text generator for UI teams. Marked for follow-up.

2026-03-05 QA note (Ruben Ortiz): Integration tests should simulate server-sent duplicate deltas and reorder; adding tests to ensure dedupe TTL doesn't cause data loss when legitimate late events arrive.

2026-03-10 Arjun Patel: Implemented initial POC. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python/pull/2748 (WIP). Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SDK/pages/stream-orchestrator-spec. Dev Console trace: https://console.redwood/dev/traces/stream-orch-61111

2026-03-12 Sofia Mendes: API review comments addressed: renamed resume_policy -> resume_mode, added resume_attempts backoff policy, and simplified telemetry hook signature to accept typed enums. Preparing for internal beta.
2026-03-12 Arjun Patel: Packaging note - ensure py.typed and exported names in __all__ for Sphinx autodoc. Also adding compatibility adapter for older sync helpers.
